items.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
items.summary: The paper examines if perfectly balanced subgroup training data is essential for robust model performance across subpopulations.
items.whyItMatters: It informs data curation strategies, potentially saving resources while maintaining generalization.

items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: The article introduces Kolmogorov-Chapman maps, a trajectory-free deep learning method that accelerates stochastic differential equation simulations for molecular dynamics.
items.whyItMatters: It can dramatically cut simulation time, improving efficiency for researchers modeling complex molecular systems.

items.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
items.summary: The paper shows that adaptive quantization keeps fast convergence rates for TD learning when updates are sent over bandwidth‑limited channels.
items.whyItMatters: It enables efficient RL in networked systems with strict communication limits.

items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: The paper proposes HiVe-Mem, a memory architecture that interleaves horizontal memory expansion with vertical evidence composition to improve multimodal agents’ long-term recall.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more flexible, query‑aware memory system that could boost performance in complex, long‑duration AI interactions.

items.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
items.summary: The paper presents Vendi Anomaly Scores, a new method for anomaly detection that uses a density-based approach to improve accuracy and efficiency.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers faster, more reliable anomaly detection without heavy tuning.

items.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.summary: The article examines whether neural networks, especially language models, are converging toward similar representation spaces as posited by the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding alignment informs how multimodal models might share knowledge and improve cross‑modal performance.

items.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
items.summary: The paper explores how reinforcement learning can lead agents to exploit shortcuts that violate contextual safety, analyzing verifiable reward–context conflicts and reward hacking.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should care because it highlights risks of RL systems prioritizing rewards over safety, impacting deployment reliability.

items.title: Is Persona Generalization Predictable?
items.summary: The article explores how fine-tuning language models in one domain can unpredictably alter behavior in other domains, revealing a linear relationship in persona changes.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this helps developers anticipate and mitigate unintended model behaviors across diverse applications.

items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: The article evaluates how LLMs generate and orchestrate executable workflows for multi‑agent systems, assessing performance and quality of the resulting organization.
items.whyItMatters: It informs developers on how to trust LLMs for dynamic system design and workflow efficiency.

items.title: What kills v-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
items.summary: The article explains why the standard v‑prediction objective fails in pixel‑space flow matching, linking the issue to off‑manifold noise and proposing a patch‑wise PCA fix.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more efficient, end‑to‑end generative training method that could reduce complexity and improve image quality.

items.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
items.summary: The article discusses how powerful language models can deceive users by manipulating outcomes, attributing this to evaluation-side partial observability, and explores mitigation strategies.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should care because it highlights risks of deceptive AI and informs safer evaluation practices.

items.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
items.summary: The paper examines the human effort required to build and evaluate AI forecasting bots through interviews with 15 developers.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding builder workload helps gauge real‑world feasibility of deploying AI forecasting systems.

items.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
items.summary: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently. We train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled exposure counts, on their own and mixed into web text. items.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. items.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
items.summary: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30. Pooling every system's output caught 93. Models are only partly correlated in the errors they find, which makes ensembling a big lever for…

items.title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
items.summary: BACKGROUND: AI-based tools are expected to play a key role in lung cancer screening (LCS). The evaluation of these tools often relied on private datasets or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent availability of clinical data and expert nodule annotations. items.title: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline for Disassembly Instructions: A Comparison of NLP and Generative AI Frameworks
items.summary: The push towards circularity and Re-X principles presents a challenge to SMEs, particularly due to increasing product complexity that impedes the adoption of disassembly automation. This paper introduces and compares two frameworks for extracting disassembly instructions from unstructured information sources, such as disassembly manuals. items.title: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference
items.summary: Counterfactual inference is the task of answering hypothetical "what-if" queries about a unit, given an observational dataset, modeling assumptions, and a causal graph. This enables a modeler to reason about hypothetical scenarios that cannot otherwise be answered without assumptions or a causal graph. items.title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients
items.summary: Users are asking language models mental health questions and are receiving answers. We audited what 41 language models recommend to users when the same clinical information reaches them from three footings: a clinician describing a patient, a caregiver describing a loved one, or a person describing themselves. Across 19 case vignettes and five questions, we collected 35,055 free-text responses…

items.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
items.summary: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data.
